natural_body: 40% SMB discount: signup +31%, revenue +18%, but retention -12%; no renewal.

first.rationale:
The two live deficits are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the intervention should attack the funnel, not the price. memory_73 is already specific enough not to need a pull: the 40% SMB discount bought signup and short-run revenue while destroying retention, which is exactly the wrong trade against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, even under competitive price pressure. memory_57 (referrals) and memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) are plausible but address segments that are not currently degrading; they do not touch the measured decline. That leaves simplify_onboarding versus activation_messaging. I choose onboarding because memory_86 claims a lift in completion AND time-to-value, which is upstream of activation and would plausibly move both declining metrics, whereas memory_91 moves only week-one engagement.

I am spending both verification pulls on the memories I actually intend to act on, not on the one I intend to reject. memory_86 and memory_31 are the load-bearing claims, and both are stated in proxy terms — 'activation', 'completion', 'adoption' — with no retention or revenue figure attached, which is precisely the gap that made memory_73 look good at day 31 before renewal data arrived. I want the original records to check three things: whether the lift survived past week one, whether any revenue or retention metric was tracked at all, and whether 'cutting required fields' removed qualification data (firmographics, use-case, seat count) that downstream routing and sales depend on.

That last point is the main downstream risk and I am flagging it explicitly: stripping signup fields can raise activation counts while lowering the qualified share of the funnel, so the metric improves as the business worsens. Same failure shape as the discount. So I run this as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout, with retention and qualified-revenue-per-cohort as guardrails alongside completion, and I hold the inherited claims as promising-but-unconfirmed until the archive shows what was actually measured. If verification reveals the lifts were proxy-only or came from removing qualification data, I fall back to activation_messaging, which improves engagement without degrading the intake record.
